title: WPMS/1949/2020 of MOH SHAKIR Vs BANK OF BARODA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1949 of 2020
Moh Shakir and Another
 ...Petitioners
Vs.
Bank of Baroda and Others
...Respondents
Mr. Atul Kumar Bansal, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Siddharth Jain, Advocate for respondent no. 1.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
The matter is heard through video conferencing.
2. The respondent no. 2, who admittedly happens to be the
principal borrower and defaulter of the loan amount, due to be paid by
him to the financial institution of respondent no. 1; on initiation of the
proceedings, under Section 13 of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, had
initiated the proceedings under Section 17(1), by approaching before
the Debt Recovery Tribunal; by initiating the proceedings by way of
S.A. No. 70 of 2020 'M/s Akeel Traders & Ors. Vs. A.O. Bank of
Baroda' on 24.08.2020. Prior to initiation of proceedings under
Section 17(1) and later during its pendency, the respondent no. 1, had
proceeded with the auction proceedings in pursuance to the prior Sale
Notice dated 10.07.2020, as well as the Auction dated 28.07.2020.
The said matter and issue was also made as a subject matter of
consideration before the Tribunal, when the Tribunal has passed the
impugned order on 28.08.2020.
3. During the intervening proceedings, which were being
held before the Debt Recovery Tribunal; an issue crept-in that the
petitioner who is the auction purchaser and who submits that in
pursuance to the conclusion of the auction proceedings dated
28.07.2020 in his favour, the sale certificate has already been issued in
his favour on 20.08.2020 and he claims that the physical possession of
the secured asset thus auctioned, is also alleged to have been handed
over to him. However, in the proceedings before the Debt Recovery

2
Tribunal, the respondent no. 2, i.e. the principal defaulter/borrower,
had submitted that the auction purchaser, i.e. the petitioner herein, is
required to be impleaded as a party respondent to the proceedings
under Section 17(1) of the Act, pending before the Debt Recovery
Tribunal and, accordingly, the Debt Recovery Tribunal has passed an
order directing the applicant to take steps for amending the pleading
of the proceedings of the Debt Recovery Tribunal, in SA No. 70 of
2020 by impleading the auction purchaser, i.e. the petitioner, as a
party to the proceeding, and the following order has passed:
"In view of above, the Respondent-Bank is directed to
provide the details of auction purchaser to the Applicants
through both modes within three days.
In case, the Applicants take steps for
amendment/impleadment of Auction Purchaser within 7 days,
registry shall issue the summons to the Auction Purchaser and
Applicants shall serve the summons by Registered AD
Cover/Speed Post AD Cover/Dasti Mode/Dasti Mode against
acknowledgement as well as through e-mail.
Further, the Applicants are directed to place the proof
of details of prospective buyers who offered Rs. 24.00 lacs
for the purchase of secured asset along with proof of deposit
of said amount by 25.09.2020.
In case, the Applicants or prospective buyers deposit
any such amount, the Respondent-Bank shall accept the same
and keep the same in no lien account in which interest is
payable. However, this order shall not create any right either
in favour of Applicants or prospective buyer by depositing the
amount with the Respondent-Bank.
Meanwhile, status quo qua physical possession of
secured asset as well as further alienation of the same be
maintained by all the parties including auction purchaser till
the next date of hearing.
The Respondent-Bank is directed to serve the copy of
today's order upon the Auction Purchaser within three days
through both modes.
Registry is directed to provide the scanned copy of this
order to all the parties through e-mail and also upload on the
official website of DRT.
Re-listed on 29.09.2020 through video conferencing
for further consideration."
4. Looking to the nature and the order thus passed where a
direction has been issued to the respondent no. 2, to implead the
auction purchaser, i.e. the petitioner, and directing the matter to be re-listed on 29.09.2020, and further directed the parties to maintain the
status-quo; qua the physical possession of the secured asset would
take the shape of the order to be an interlocutory order passed in the

3
pending proceeding of SA No. 70 of 2020 'M/s Akeel Traders & Ors.
Vs. A.O. Bank of Baroda', under Section 17(1) of the Act, which was
passed by way of an interim arrangement.
5. The petitioner has preferred this writ petition, assailing
the said order dated 28.08.2020. The Registry has reported that there
is a defect and particularly the defect no. 2, was pertained to the
Article of the Constitution of India, under which the writ petition has
been filed, the said defect is over-ruled; and it is hereby directed that
the writ petition would be treated as to be a writ petition, which has
been preferred under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
6. This Court during the course of the argument had called
upon the petitioner to address the court about the implications
contained under Section 18 of the Securitization Act, which provides
for an alternative Appellate Forum, which was available to the
petitioner to approach the Appellate Tribunal as against the orders
passed by the Debt Recovery Tribunal under Section 17(1) of the Act,
which is impugned in the present writ petition. Section 18 of the
SARFAESI Act, 2002, reads as under:
"18. Appeal to Appellate Tribunal.-
(1) Any person aggrieved, by any order made by the Debts
Recovery Tribunal 1[under section 17, may prefer an appeal
along with such fee, as may be prescribed] to an Appellate
Tribunal within thirty days from the date of receipt of the order
of Debts Recovery Tribunal.-(1) Any person aggrieved, by any
order made by the Debts Recovery Tribunal 2[under section 17,
may prefer an appeal along with such fee, as may be prescribed]
to an Appellate Tribunal within thirty days from the date of
receipt of the order of Debts Recovery Tribunal." 2[Provided that
different fees may be prescribed for filing an appeal by the
borrower or by the person other than the borrower:] 3[Provided
further that no appeal shall be entertained unless the borrower
has deposited with the Appellate Tribunal fifty per cent. of the
amount of debt due from him, as claimed by the secured creditors
or determined by the Debts Recovery Tribunal, whichever is less:
Provided also that the Appellate Tribunal may, for the reasons to
be recorded in writing, reduce the amount to not less than
twenty-five per cent. of debt referred to in the second proviso.]
(2) Save as otherwise provided in this Act, the Appellate
Tribunal shall, as far as may be, dispose of the appeal in
accordance with the provisions of the Recovery of Debts Due to
Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (51 of 1993) and rules
made thereunder."

4
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner had submitted that the
platform, which has been provided under Section 18 of the Act of
2002, would not be available to him because he is not an, 'aggrieved
person'. This aspect has been argued by the learned counsel Mr. A.K.
Bansal, under the pretext that since the action has proceeded under
Section 13 (8) and since it was not a proceeding, which was drawn
under Section 13 of the Act against him and, hence, the decision taken
by the Debt Recovery Tribunal, though it falls to be under Section17,
but he would not be an aggrieved person, as defined therein because
approaching to DRT by aggrieved person would be the person against
whom action under Section 13 has been resorted to by the secured
creditor, which would be respondent no. 2 only, hence, Section 18
remedy is not available to him as in fact he is only the auction
purchaser.
8. If the simplicitor language of Section 17 is taken into
consideration, the right to approach the Debt Recovery Tribunal, has
been opened to any person (including borrower) for any action, which
has taken by the secured creditor under Section 13(4) of the Act. I am
of the view that, the provisions of Section 13(8) is procedural in
nature and it is not a substantive provision; where an action has been
taken against the principal borrower and if the language of Section 18
is taken into consideration, I am of the opinion that it contemplates a
right, which has been granted by law to any aggrieved person, by any
order, which is made by the Debt Recovery Tribunal under Section
17, its he who may prefer an appeal under Section 18 of the Act,
before Appellate Tribunal, and it has got no nexus that there has had
to be a prior action against that person, who is approaching before the
Appellate Tribunal under Section 18; to have suffered from a prior
action under Section 13 of the Act. Unlike Section 17, Section 18 does
not speak about that there has had to be a prior action against the
aggrieved person under Section 13, in order to enable him to approach
the Appellate Tribunal under Section 18 of the Act; rather Section 18
simplicitor says that "any person by any order made by the Debt
Recovery Tribunal can approach to the Appellate Tribunal", it is not
qualified by a prior action as mandatory under Section 13 of the Act,

5
to invoke Section 18, as it has been mandated for Section 17 of the
Act of 2002.
9. In the present case, by virtue of the impugned order, the
respondent no. 2, who is the applicant to the proceedings under
Section 17, had sought an impleadment of the petitioner, who is the
auction purchaser, to be made as a party to the proceedings and an
interim order has been granted. This Court is of the view that there are
two remedies, which are available to the petitioner, either he should
await his impleadment in the proceedings for the purposes of issuance
of notice to him, or, in an alternative, he himself can get himself
impleaded because he claims himself to be the auction purchaser of
the property in question to whom the possession has already been
handed over. In case if he chooses not to be impleaded as a party to
the proceeding and still he alleges to be aggrieved by the direction
issued to implead him as party in the pending proceedings under
Section 17, in that eventuality, the impugned order dated 28.08.2020,
would fall to be the order, which has been passed by the Debt
Recovery Tribunal under Section 17 and since the said order has got
no relationship, as already held above, to be emanating from Section
13 of the Act, the remedy available to the petitioner would be to
approach the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal, under Section 18 of
the Act. Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner has prayed that, in
case, if the petitioner approaches the Debt Recovery Appellate
Tribunal, under Section 18, within a period of one month from the
date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment, the Debt
Recovery Appellate Tribunal, would liberally construe the aspect of
limitation.
10. Accordingly, this Court declines to exercise its
extraordinary supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the
Constitution of India as against the interlocutory order dated
28.08.2020, because the appropriate legal appellate forum is still
available to the petitioner under Section 18 of the Act of 2002, as
dealt with above.

6
11. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed due to
availability of a statutory remedy to the petitioner under the Act of
2002.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 29.10.2020
Pooja
